title: Taste the sweetness hidden in the fortress
summary: The Lord is already within the body-fortress, but stubbornness cannot taste Him. Mercy opens the Guru's Shabad until nearness becomes something the heart can actually taste.
takeaway: Ask mercy to make the hidden Lord tasteable again.
lifeApplication: When your heart is closed and unimpressed, stop pretending distance is honesty. Ask for mercy plainly, read the line slowly, and notice one place where the day can be answered with sweetness.

source.shortMeaning: The Lord dwells within the body-fortress, and mercy through the Guru's Shabad lets the stubborn heart finally taste Him.
source.lifeApplication: Ask for mercy where you feel spiritually dull, then give one slow line of Shabad enough attention to become taste rather than information.

evidence.coreClaim: The problem is not the Lord's absence but the heart's untasting stubbornness; mercy through the Guru's Shabad makes hidden sweetness real.
evidence.turn: Ask for the mercy that changes nearness from a doctrine into a tasted sweetness.
evidence.practicalImplication: When your heart is closed and unimpressed, stop pretending distance is honesty. Ask for mercy plainly, read the line slowly, and notice one place where the day can be answered with sweetness.
